control_record.verifies: the band-3 reading of the 318 bookends after amendments 2-3 (option A + the tie-break): where the +11% goes

explanation: Option A (amendment 3) is the whole remaining increase, now +3.4% total, band 2. (1) The gap pass costs what it must: its chord test is vectorized (round 3) and its flood, way_out and trace read lists instead of arrays (round 4), both byte-identical; seed 25 and 39 each grow only +0.2-0.4 s in homesteads, the pass, against the control's 0.7-1.0 s before either fix (perf-318-control-gap-pass). (2) Seed 4 at 15 households (+17.6%: web +0.4 s, hinterland +0.3 s) and notice on 20/47 (+0.7 s) and 40/39 (+2.2 s) are the 20 ft homestead gap moving the layout, not added work: in the control, with main's gap and the gap pass kept, seed 4's web returns to 0.56 s and hinterland to 0.90 s (main's 0.69 and 0.92), and notice drops to 0.22 / 0.26 s - while the same swap raises notice on 15/4 (0.28 -> 0.77 s) and 15/39 (0.10 -> 0.61 s). The board's search and the web's settling are a lottery over where the houses fall. The tie-break makes seating itself cheaper than main: 40 households -11.5%, 20 households -0.4%, 10 households +0.8%.
